The Artemis II crew successfully splashed down in the Pacific Ocean off the coast of San Diego, California, on Friday, April 10, 2026, at 8:07 p.m. ET (0007 GMT April 11), concluding a historic 10-day mission. The crew safely returned after traveling around the Moon, with recovery teams extracting them shortly after, marking the first crewed lunar mission return since 1972. Key Artemis II Landing Details: Mission Goal: A successful 10-day lunar flyby, testing Orion’s systems and paving the way for future Artemis moon landings. Splashdown Time: Friday, April 10, 2026, at 8:07 p.m. EDT (0007 GMT April 11). Location: Pacific Ocean off the coast of San Diego, California. Crew: NASA astronauts Reid Wiseman (commander), Victor Glover (pilot), Christina Koch (mission specialist), and CSA (Canadian Space Agency) astronaut Jeremy Hansen (mission specialist). Recovery: The crew was extracted from the Orion capsule via helicopter and brought to the USS John P. Murtha. Descent Highlights: The capsule passed through 1000 ft before successfully executing a splashdown after a 694,481-mile journey. Parachutes were deployed in sequence—drogues followed by three main parachutes—reducing speed to approximately 20 mph (32 km/h). The "perfect" mission concluded without incident, with teams confirming the integrity of the capsule following a precise descent.
